intro: Whether you're purchasing your first home in Baltimore, relocating to Frederick or exploring properties in Annapolis, Rockville or another Maryland community, understanding your monthly housing costs can help you establish a realistic purchase budget.

Our free Maryland mortgage calculator estimates your monthly mortgage payment based on the home price, down payment, interest rate and repayment term. Include property taxes, homeowners insurance, private mortgage insurance and association fees to compare financing options before making an offer.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Maryland?

blocks.markdown:
A $420,000 Maryland home purchased with a 20% down payment and a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $2,014.49.

This example assumes no private mortgage insurance. The interest rate, property taxes, insurance premiums and association fees are illustrative assumptions rather than current statewide averages.

Maryland offers a diverse housing market that includes Baltimore's urban neighborhoods, Washington metropolitan area suburbs, Chesapeake Bay communities and rural properties in western Maryland.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Maryland QuickFacts](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/MD/SBO060222), the median value of owner-occupied homes was $419,900 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs for households with mortgages were $2,347, while the owner-occupied housing rate was 67.6%.

These historical statistics provide a useful affordability benchmark but do not represent current property listing prices.

Homes in Montgomery County or communities near Washington, DC, may have substantially different purchase prices from properties in western Maryland.

Research comparable sales in your preferred neighborhood and investigate local tax rates, commuting expenses and insurance premiums before determining your purchase budget.

sections.heading: How to Use the Maryland Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Enter the expected purchase price of your property and your available down payment.

Select your preferred mortgage term and enter the annual interest rate quoted by your lender.

Next, include estimated annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and monthly HOA or condominium association fees.

If your conventional mortgage requires private mortgage insurance, include that expense.

Review the monthly payment breakdown to understand the contribution of each expense.

You can change the purchase price, down payment or repayment period to compare financing scenarios without submitting a mortgage application.

The amortization schedule also shows how much interest you may pay and how your outstanding mortgage balance decreases over time.

sections.heading: How Maryland Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Maryland property taxes generally depend on assessed property values and applicable state, county and municipal tax rates.

The State Department of Assessments and Taxation, commonly known as SDAT, handles real property assessments.

Local governments establish their respective tax rates, which can differ considerably between jurisdictions.

The [Maryland property tax rate directory](https://dat.maryland.gov/pages/tax-rates.aspx) publishes updated rates and local homestead credit caps, including information for the 2026–2027 tax year.

### Maryland's property assessment cycle

Maryland generally reassesses real property on a three-year cycle.

When an assessment increases, the difference between the previous and new values is normally phased in over three years.

The [SDAT property assessment guidance](https://dat.maryland.gov/realproperty/Pages/Questions-and-Answers-About-Real-Property-Assessments.aspx) explains how phased-in values work.

### Maryland Homestead Property Tax Credit

The [Maryland Homestead Property Tax Credit](https://dat.maryland.gov/realproperty/pages/maryland-homestead-tax-credit.aspx) helps eligible homeowners manage increases in taxable assessments on their principal residences.

The state portion generally uses a 10% annual limit. Counties and municipalities can establish lower limits.

This credit does not prevent the property's market value from increasing, nor does it guarantee that the total annual tax bill cannot rise by more than the applicable percentage.

Changes in tax rates and other charges can still affect the final bill.

Homeowners must establish eligibility through an application. Buyers should not assume they will automatically receive the previous owner's accumulated credit.

### Homeowners' Property Tax Credit

Maryland also provides a separate income-based property tax relief program.

The [Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program](https://dat.maryland.gov/realproperty/Pages/Homeowners%27-Property-Tax-Credit-Program.aspx) evaluates eligible household income and qualifying property taxes.

Its published guidance includes a maximum combined gross household income of $60,000, subject to additional eligibility requirements and limitations.

This program differs from the Homestead Credit. Confirm qualification before deducting any expected benefit from your mortgage estimate.

Insurance premiums depend on your property's construction, location, replacement cost, condition and selected coverage.

Maryland properties may face thunderstorms, coastal flooding, tropical storms and winter weather.

Obtain insurance quotes before completing your purchase.

### Chesapeake Bay and coastal insurance

Homes near the Chesapeake Bay, tidal rivers and Atlantic coastline may face greater exposure to storm surge and flooding.

Standard homeowners insurance generally excludes flooding.

Use the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) to investigate your property's flood exposure.

Depending on your lender and property location, separate flood insurance may be required.

Include its annual premium when estimating total housing expenses.

### Windstorm deductibles

The [Maryland Insurance Administration's storm insurance guidance](https://insurance.maryland.gov/Consumer/Pages/Automobile-and-Homeowners-Post-Disaster-Claim-FAQs.aspx) explains that some policies contain separate deductibles for wind-related losses.

These deductibles may be calculated as a percentage of insured dwelling value rather than a fixed dollar amount.

For example, a 2% deductible on $400,000 of dwelling coverage would equal $8,000 for a covered claim to which that deductible applies.

Compare insurance premiums alongside coverage limits and potential out-of-pocket costs.

The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development administers the Maryland Mortgage Program, commonly called MMP.

### MMP 1st Time Advantage

The [1st Time Advantage program](https://mmp.maryland.gov/home-loans/mmp-1st-time-advantage) provides eligible first-time buyers with mortgage financing and optional purchase assistance.

Available options include:

The assistance arrangements generally involve zero-interest deferred second mortgages.

Repayment becomes due under specified conditions, including repayment or refinancing of the primary mortgage, property sale or ownership transfer.

These arrangements should not be treated as unconditional grants.

### Maryland Flex Loans

The [MMP Flex Loan program](https://mmp.maryland.gov/home-loans/mmp-flex-loans) serves qualifying first-time and repeat buyers.

Available assistance options include the Flex 6000 product and a second mortgage equal to 3% of the first mortgage amount.

Applicants must satisfy income, credit, homebuyer education and property eligibility requirements.

Compare the associated first mortgage rate alongside the assistance amount.

### Partner Match assistance

Maryland's [down payment assistance directory](https://mmp.maryland.gov/home-loans/down-payment-assistance) explains that qualifying participants using designated $6,000 assistance products may receive matching funds of up to $2,500 through approved partners.

Local governments, employers and participating organizations may also offer separate purchase assistance.

Confirm program compatibility, eligibility and funding availability with an approved lender before incorporating assistance into your purchase budget.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a Maryland Home

blocks.markdown:
Homebuyers should investigate commuting expenses, particularly when purchasing outside major employment centers.

Rail fares, tolls, parking and vehicle maintenance can significantly affect the financial advantages of a lower purchase price.

Condominium and townhouse buyers should review association fees, reserve funds and potential special assessments.

Ask which expenses are covered through association dues to avoid double-counting insurance or maintenance costs.

Also prepare for closing expenses, including applicable transfer and recordation taxes, title services, inspections and lender fees.

Review the [CFPB's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/) before accepting a mortgage offer.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Maryland?

blocks.markdown:
Begin with your reliable monthly take-home income and subtract existing debt payments, household expenses and regular savings contributions.

Use our [Maryland Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/maryland-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate after-tax earnings and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate existing borrowing obligations.

Allow sufficient room for insurance deductibles, home repairs, transportation and emergency savings.

A lender's mortgage approval does not necessarily indicate that the approved payment will be comfortable for your household.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $420,000 Maryland home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $2,014.49. Taxes, insurance and applicable fees increase your total housing payment.

### How does Maryland's Homestead Property Tax Credit work?

The credit limits qualifying annual increases in taxable assessments on eligible principal residences. The state generally uses a 10% limit, while local governments may establish lower limits. Homeowners must meet applicable eligibility requirements.

### Does Maryland offer down payment assistance for homebuyers?

Yes. The Maryland Mortgage Program offers assistance through its 1st Time Advantage and Flex products. Assistance may be a fixed dollar amount or a percentage of the first mortgage, generally structured as deferred secondary financing.
